Definition: something preserved, i.e. the settlings (plural only) of wine
BiblicalUsage: Lees are what settles at the bottom of the wine, and the word is used for men who have settled too long. Isaiah promises a feast of wines on the lees, well refined, but Moab has settled on his lees and has not been emptied from vessel to vessel, so his taste remained in him. The psalm warns that the dregs of the cup are for the wicked, and Zephaniah punishes the men settled on their lees who say the LORD will not do good.
TheologicalSignificance: I believe settling is the danger in this word. Wine must be poured off its lees or it sours, and men must be emptied and poured again, and I hold that God refines His people by moving them.
